items.title: ‘It doesn’t seem fair’: I’m retired and have plenty of money. Why can’t I qualify for a retail credit card?
items.content: “I draw from my IRA as needed for household repairs, trips and other larger expenses.”

items.title: Here’s where thousands of homeowners face higher insurance bills after FEMA updated its flood maps
items.content: The federal government redrew flood maps across America this summer — and it could mean bigger housing bills for homeowners who now live in newly designated flood zones.

items.title: Palantir’s stock is heading for its highest close of the year, in a dramatic comeback
items.content: Palantir’s last earnings report reignited investor enthusiasm, and now the company is basking in the glow of a real-world AI boom.

items.title: The ingredients for a financial reckoning are all in place
items.content: A witch’s brew of rising debt levels, higher costs of capital and contagion risks is bubbling.

items.title: This test screens for 50 cancers — but whether Medicare and other health insurers will cover it hinges on FDA approval
items.content: Grail’s Galleri test looks for 50 cancers from a blood draw, but a major study failed to prove it could detect later-stage cancers.

items.title: Businesses are growing at the fastest pace in over four years. Why war and inflation aren’t stopping the U.S. economy.
items.content: Expensive gas, higher inflation, a stalemate with Iran and rising interest rates — no matter. The U.S. economy appears to have sped up in the early fall.

items.title: McDonald’s is making a historic bet on chicken — and AI — to bring back customers
items.content: Investors aren’t sold on plans to introduce new McNugget flavors, and an analyst recently noted that McDonald’s has struggled to break through on chicken-related innovation.

items.title: ‘She says it’s just money’: My friend pays for everything. I should be grateful, but I can’t stand her anymore.
items.content: “On each of these weekends away, she’s probably spending $500.”

items.title: Bond yields surge to 5.12% as Wall Street fears more Fed rate hikes
items.content: Stocks fall, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 retreating from record territory as bond yields suddenly jump.

items.title: Fuel prices keep rising — and so do Democrats’ chances of winning both the House and Senate
items.content: Losses for President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterms are expected in large part because of voters’ frustrations with the elevated cost of living.
